In mathematics, '''Topological Hochschild homology''' is a topological refinement of [[Hochschild homology]] which rectifies some technical issues with computations in characteristic <math>p</math>. For instance, if we consider the <math>\mathbb{Z}</math>-algebra <math>\mathbb{F}_p</math> then <blockquote><math>HH_k(\mathbb{F}_p/\mathbb{Z}) \cong \begin{cases}
\mathbb{F}_p & k \text{ even} \\
0 & k \text{ odd}
\end{cases}</math> </blockquote>but <u>if we consider the ring structure</u> on <blockquote><math>\begin{align}
HH_*(\mathbb{F}_p/\mathbb{Z}) &= \mathbb{F}_p\langle u \rangle \\
&= \mathbb{F}_p[u,u^2/2!, u^3/3!,\ldots]

\end{align}</math> </blockquote>(as a [[Divided power structure|divided power algebra]] structure) then there is a significant technical issue: if we set <math>u \in HH_2(\mathbb{F}_p/\mathbb{Z})</math>, so <math>u^2 \in HH_4(\mathbb{F}_p/\mathbb{Z})</math>, and so on, we have <math>u^p = 0</math> from the resolution of <math>\mathbb{F}_p</math> as an algebra over <math>\mathbb{F}_p\otimes^\mathbf{L}\mathbb{F}_p</math>,<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Krause |first1=Achim |last2=Nikolaus |first2=Thomas |date= |title=Lectures on Topological Hochschild Homology and Cyclotomic Spectra |url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/IVV5WS/WebHop/user/nikolaus/papers.html |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date= |website=}}</ref> i.e. <blockquote><math>HH_k(\mathbb{F}_p/\mathbb{Z}) = H_k(\mathbb{F}_p\otimes_{
    \mathbb{F}_p\otimes^\mathbf{L}\mathbb{F}_p
}\mathbb{F}_p)</math> </blockquote>This calculation is further elaborated on the [[Hochschild homology]] page, but the key point is the pathological behavior of the ring structure on the Hochschild homology of <math>\mathbb{F}_p</math>. In contrast, the Topological Hochschild Homology ring has the isomorphism <blockquote><math>THH_*(\mathbb{F}_p) = \mathbb{F}_p[u]</math> </blockquote>giving a less pathological theory. Moreover, this calculation forms the basis of many other THH calculations, such as for smooth algebras <math>A/\mathbb{F}_p</math>

== Construction ==
Recall that the [[Eilenberg–MacLane spectrum]] can be embed ring objects in the [[derived category]] of the integers <math>D(\mathbb{Z})</math> into [[ring spectrum]] over the ring spectrum of the [[stable homotopy group of spheres]]. This makes it possible to take a commutative ring <math>A</math> and constructing a complex analogous to the Hochschild complex using the monoidal product in ring spectra, namely, <math>\wedge_\mathbb{S}</math> acts formally like the derived tensor product <math>\otimes^\mathbf{L}</math> over the integers. We define the Topological Hochschild complex of <math>A</math> (which could be a commutative [[differential graded algebra]], or just a [[commutative algebra]]) as the [[simplicial complex]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Morrow|first=Matthew|date=|title=Topological Hochschild homology in arithmetic geometry|url=https://www.math.arizona.edu/~swc/aws/2019/2019MorrowNotes.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201224194152/https://www.math.arizona.edu/~swc/aws/2019/2019MorrowNotes.pdf|archive-date=24 Dec 2020|access-date=|website=}}</ref> <sup>pg 33-34</sup> called the [[Bar complex]]<blockquote><math>\cdots \to HA\wedge_\mathbb{S}HA\wedge_\mathbb{S}HA \to HA\wedge_\mathbb{S}HA \to  HA
</math></blockquote>of spectra (note that the arrows are incorrect because of Wikipedia formatting...). Because simplicial objects in spectra have a realization as a spectrum, we form the spectrum<blockquote><math>THH(A) \in \text{Spectra}</math></blockquote>which has homotopy groups <math>\pi_i(THH(A)) </math> defining the topological Hochschild homology of the ring object <math>A</math>.
